cita: Li, R., Zhang, Z., Bo, X., Tian, Z., Chen, X., Dai, Q., Dong, Z. y Tang, R. (2025). CAM: A Constructivist View of Agentic Memory for LLM-Based Reading Comprehension.
problema: LLMs are overwhelmed by the information volume of long-form documents, and current agentic memory approaches only mimic human memory at a superficial level, lacking a coherent design principle for how memory should be structured, assimilated, and adapted as new content arrives.
mecanismo: Drawing on Piaget's Constructivist Theory: raw text chunks form a foundational semantic network (assimilation) via a local-first incremental overlapping clustering algorithm (ego-centric node replication + incremental label propagation) that lets each low-level chunk belong to multiple higher-level abstractions (a many-to-many mapping), while higher-level nodes are recursively LLM-summarized into a hierarchy (WRITE/CONSOLIDACION); only the locally-affected part of the hierarchy is updated or rebalanced when new batches of chunks arrive, never a full reconstruction (accommodation, ACTUALIZACION), enabling efficient online-batch integration; retrieval uses a Prune-and-Grow associative strategy: fast cosine-similarity localization of candidate nodes followed by LLM-guided recursive expansion along same-layer and child links.
evaluacion: Single-document (NovelQA question answering, QMSum summarization, FABLES claim verification) and multi-document (MultiHop-RAG QA, ODSum-Story/Meeting summarization) benchmarks vs FullContext/MemGPT/ReadAgent (unstructured) and RAPTOR/GraphRAG/HippoRAG/MemTree (structured) baselines; a batch-level online setting measuring integration efficiency.
numeros_clave: CAM improves ACC-L by +4.5 on NovelQA, +3.7 on QMSum, +4.3/+4.0 F1P/F1N on FABLES over the best baseline (Table 2); batch integration is over 4x faster than existing methods (Sec 5.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: CAM's hierarchical schema of raw chunks incrementally aggregated into LLM-summarized abstractions (Sec 3.1, Eq.1) is a concrete instance of a derived, multi-level cache MF's TIER-INDICE anchor could adopt for its own index tier.

Dynamic accommodation -- locally rebalancing only the affected part of the memory hierarchy rather than reconstructing it wholesale (Sec 3.3) -- is a directly reusable pattern for MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor to keep promotion of gotchas into recipes cheap and incremental.

CAM reports over 4x faster batch integration than existing offline/entry-wise-online methods (Sec 5.3), a concrete efficiency gain from a structured, incrementally-updatable memory design relevant to MF's COSTO anchor.

notes: Numbers Table 2 (reading comprehension) + Sec 5.3 (batch integration speed). plan_estado=NO.

cita: Lu and Li (2025). Dynamic Affective Memory Management for Personalized LLM Agents.
problema: RAG-based personalized-agent memories suffer from 'memory stagnation' (storing contradictory sentiment facts as isolated, immutable records instead of an evolving belief) and 'memory bloat' (indiscriminate storage of every interaction inflates retrieval latency, cost and noise).
mecanismo: Each memory unit represents a user's sentiment toward a specific object-aspect as a confidence distribution (positive/negative/neutral), updated via a Bayesian-inspired weighted-average rule (Cnew=(C*W+S*P)/(W+S)) that treats new evidence as an incremental weight rather than a discrete overwrite (WRITE/ACTUALIZACION); a Master Agent decides to Store/Integrate/Abandon new evidence based on the resulting belief entropy of the update (ADMISION/CONSOLIDACION), and memory units with persistently high entropy and low weight are actively Deleted (OLVIDO) via entropy-driven compression to counter memory bloat.
evaluacion: A purpose-built DABench benchmark (2,500 observation sequences, 100 simulated 1,000-turn sessions, 500 query-memory pairs) targeting affective expression/change; a 500-observation memory-growth ablation with/without the Bayesian update; a stabilization analysis over 30 sequential observations of a single object/aspect.
numeros_clave: Confidence rapidly initializes within ~10-15 observations and converges as evidence accumulates (Sec 4.3.3); Bayesian-update compression reduces total memory size by 63.7%-70.6% after 500 dialogue turns vs vanilla-RAG memory management, stabilizing at 130-140 units (Sec 4.4.1, Figure 7); the system matches or beats baselines on personalization/coherence while retaining only ~40% of the memory units (Sec 4.4.2, Table 2).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: Modeling each fact as a Bayesian confidence distribution rather than a discrete immutable record (Sec 3.4.2) is a concrete anti-drift mechanism -- contradictory observations reweight belief instead of creating silently conflicting records -- directly relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor (staleness/poisoning).

Entropy-driven compression/deletion is measured to cut total memory size 63.7%-70.6% after 500 turns vs uncompressed storage (Figure 7), a strong quantified instance of MF's COSTO anchor on memory-store growth, not just retrieval latency.

The Master Agent's Store/Integrate/Abandon decision, triggered by the resulting belief entropy of new evidence (Sec 3.4.1), is a concrete discretionary write-trigger design directly relevant to MF's G-M1.

cita: Kim, S., Lee, Y., Kim, S., Kim, H. y Cho, S. (2025). Pre-Storage Reasoning for Episodic Memory: Shifting Inference Burden to Memory for Personalized Dialogue.
problema: Current conversational-memory systems place the burden of complex cross-session reasoning (synthesis, temporal/causal continuity) on response-generation time, making performance heavily dependent on model size and creating computational inefficiency, especially for multi-hop and temporal-reasoning questions.
mecanismo: Conversation sessions are extracted into typed episodic memory fragments (factual/experiential/subjective) with a structured 4-pattern temporal representation -- ongoing, specific past, unclear past, and future plan (WRITE); fragments are embedded and clustered per session, then a persistent cross-session cluster pool is matched via cosine similarity to find connected pairs across sessions (CONSOLIDACION); for each connected pair, an LLM performs 'pre-storage reasoning' over 5 cognitive-schema evolution patterns (extension, accumulation, refinement, transformation, connection/implication) and writes the result as new reasoning-memory fragments BEFORE any query arrives, shifting reasoning cost from inference time to storage time (ACTUALIZACION).
evaluacion: LongMemEval and LoCoMo benchmarks across multiple model sizes/families (Qwen2.5, Gemma3, gpt-4.1) vs turn-level/session-level baselines, SeCom, HippoRAG-2, and A-Mem; a dedicated small-model comparison (PREMem plus a small model vs baselines plus a larger model); an ablation removing Step 1 (extraction) and Step 2 (pre-storage reasoning).
numeros_clave: PREMem with Qwen2.5-14B scores 64.7 on LongMemEval (LLM-judge) vs next-best A-Mem 53.6 using the larger 72B model (Table 2/3); PREMem with gpt-4.1-nano (58.7) beats all baselines using the larger gpt-4.1-base backbone (Table 3); ablation: removing Step 1 (memory extraction) drops scores by 32.7%-69.0% (Sec 4.4, Table 4).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: PREMem's temporal-representation scheme explicitly encodes future plans ('After [message-date]') as a first-class fragment category alongside facts and experiences (Sec 3.1), directly relevant to MF's PLAN-ESTADO anchor.

Shifting cross-session synthesis to pre-storage time via the 5 schema-evolution patterns (Sec 3.2.2) is measured to substantially improve downstream performance and even let small models match large-model baselines (Table 3), strong evidence for MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor of investing in write-time reasoning.

By moving reasoning to storage time, PREMem lets small models (<=4B/nano) match or beat much larger baseline models (Table 3), a concrete demonstration that upfront consolidation cost reduces inference-time cost/model-size requirements, aligning with MF's COSTO anchor.

notes: Numbers Table 2/3 (main results, small-model comparison) + Table 4 (ablation). plan_estado=SI justified by the explicit future-plan temporal category (Sec 3.1).

cita: Kang, J., Ji, M., Zhao, Z. y Bai, T. (2025). Memory OS of AI Agent.
problema: LLMs' fixed context windows and inadequate memory management cause a severe shortage of long-term memory and limited personalization, and existing memory mechanisms (knowledge-organization, retrieval-oriented, architecture-driven) each address only a single dimension in isolation rather than offering a unified, systematic memory-management framework.
mecanismo: Conversations are stored as dialogue pages in Short-Term Memory (STM, a fixed-length FIFO queue, WRITE); when STM overflows, the oldest page migrates to Mid-Term Memory (MTM), which groups pages into topic segments via a combined semantic+keyword (Jaccard) similarity score (ACTUALIZACION); segments accumulate a Heat score (visit count + interaction volume + recency decay), and segments above a heat threshold are promoted to Long-term Personal Memory (LPM: user/agent persona traits + knowledge base) while low-heat segments are evicted, mirroring OS page-replacement (CONSOLIDACION/OLVIDO); retrieval is two-tiered in MTM (segment-then-page) plus direct STM/LPM lookups, combined into the generation prompt.
evaluacion: GVD (simulated multi-turn dialogues, 15 virtual users over 10 days) and LoCoMo (long dialogues, 4 question types) benchmarks vs TiM, MemoryBank, MemGPT, and A-Mem baselines on GPT-4o-mini and Qwen2.5-7B; an ablation removing MTM, LPM, and the dialogue-page chain; a hyperparameter sweep on top-k retrieved pages; a token/LLM-call efficiency comparison.
numeros_clave: Average improvement of 49.11% on F1 and 46.18% on BLEU-1 over baselines on LoCoMo with GPT-4o-mini (Abstract); on GVD, MemoryOS beats SOTA baseline A-Mem by 3.2% accuracy (Table 1); requires only 4.9 avg. LLM calls and 3,874 tokens vs A-Mem's 13 calls/2,712 tokens and MemGPT's 16,977 tokens (Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The three-tier STM/MTM/LPM hierarchy with segmented paging (Sec 3.2) is a directly transferable Tier-1/Tier-3 split for MF's TIER-INDICE anchor, with an explicit promotion/eviction policy rather than an ad hoc cache.

The Heat-based promotion rule (visit count + interaction volume + recency decay, Eq.4) that decides when a topic segment graduates from mid-term to durable long-term persona memory (Sec 3.3) is a concrete, quantitative consolidation policy MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could adopt.

MemoryOS is measured to use far fewer LLM calls and tokens per response than A-Mem and MemGPT while outperforming them (Table 3), directly supporting MF's COSTO anchor that structured memory can win on both quality and cost.

cita: Rajesh et al. (2025). Beyond Fact Retrieval: Episodic Memory for RAG with Generative Semantic Workspaces.
problema: Standard and structured RAG memory systems (embeddings, knowledge graphs) are tailored for fact-based retrieval over static documents and fail to build the space-time-anchored narrative representations needed to track entities, roles, and states as they evolve through episodic events (e.g. a suspect's arrest -> arraignment -> release).
mecanismo: An Operator (LLM) maps each incoming text chunk to an intermediate semantic structure of actors, roles, states, verbs/valences, and spatiotemporal coordinates -- a probabilistic model where roles modulate action-distributions, states further condition them, verbs signal role/state transitions, and explicit temporal/spatial continuity constraints regularize the mapping (WRITE); a Reconciler performs a Markovian structured update, merging the new intermediate representation into a persistent Global Semantic Workspace that enforces temporal, spatial and logical coherence across the whole corpus (CONSOLIDACION/ACTUALIZACION); retrieval matches query entities to workspace nodes, reconstructs episodic summaries for them, re-ranks by relevance, and feeds only the top summaries to the answering LLM.
evaluacion: The Episodic Memory Benchmark (EpBench-200 and EpBench-2000, 100k-1M token corpora) vs Vanilla LLM, embedding RAG, GraphRAG, HippoRAG2, and LightRAG, using LLM-as-a-Judge-derived Precision/Recall/F1 stratified by the number of cues/chapters a query requires.
numeros_clave: GSW F1=0.850 on EpBench-200 (improving overall metrics by more than 10% over the next-best method) and F1=0.773 on EpBench-2000, +15% over the strongest baseline (Table 2/Table 4); GSW improves recall by up to 20% over the next-best method on the hardest 6+ cue queries; GSW reduces query-time context tokens by 51% vs the most token-efficient baseline and ~59% vs Embedding RAG/HippoRAG2 (Sec 1, Table 3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Reconciler enforces explicit temporal/spatial/logical coherence constraints when merging new information into the persistent workspace (Sec 2.2), a concrete anti-drift/consistency-checking mechanism relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor beyond simple staleness.

GSW is measured to cut query-time context tokens by 51-59% vs strong RAG baselines while improving accuracy (Sec 1, Table 3), directly evidencing that a structured narrative representation can win on MF's cost/latency axis, not just quality.

Retrieval quality (Precision/Recall/F1, stratified by query complexity) is directly measured against multiple structured-RAG baselines (Table 2/4), aligning with MF's G-M2 measured-retrieval requirement.

notes: Numbers Table 2 (EpBench-200), Table 4 (EpBench-2000), Table 3 (token efficiency). plan_estado=NO.

cita: OPPO AI Agent Team (2025). O-Mem: Omni Memory System for Personalized, Long Horizon, Self-Evolving Agents.
problema: Existing personalized-agent memory systems rely on grouping-then-retrieval semantic clustering, which can overlook semantically-irrelevant-but-important user context (e.g. health condition when planning weekend activities) and introduces retrieval noise/latency when sub-optimal groups force retrieval across multiple clusters.
mecanismo: Each user interaction is processed by an LLM into a topic, a revealed persona attribute, and a past event, routed into three typed memory components (WRITE): Persona Memory (long-term attributes/facts, updated via an explicit Add/Ignore/Update decision plus LLM-augmented nearest-neighbor clustering to merge recurring attributes, ADMISION), Working Memory (topic->interaction index), and Episodic Memory (rare-keyword->interaction index, ACTUALIZACION); retrieval is parallel across all three components (persona similarity search + topic match + rarest-clue lookup) and concatenated for response generation, rather than a single semantic-grouping search.
evaluacion: LoCoMo, PERSONAMEM, and a new Personalized Deep Research Bench, against A-Mem, MemoryOS, Mem0, LangMem, and commercial frameworks (ZEP, Memos, OpenAI memory), reporting F1/BLEU-1, multiple-choice accuracy, and goal/content alignment, plus a latency/token Pareto-efficiency comparison (Figure 1).
numeros_clave: O-Mem 51.67% average F1 on LoCoMo with GPT-4.1 vs LangMem 48.72% (Table 2); 62.99% on PERSONAMEM vs A-Mem's previous SOTA 59.42% (Table 3, +3.5%); Figure 1 shows O-Mem achieves Pareto optimality in latency and token cost vs MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: O-Mem's three separately-typed, separately-retrieved memory components (persona/working/episodic), queried in parallel rather than through one grouped index (Sec 3.1-3.3), is a concrete single-source-per-fact-type seam design directly relevant to MF's COSTURAS anchor.
O-Mem is measured to achieve Pareto-optimal latency and token cost against MemoryOS/A-Mem/Mem0 (Figure 1), a direct quantified instance of MF's COSTO anchor.

Persona attribute merging uses an explicit Add/Ignore/Update decision plus nearest-neighbor clustering of recurring attributes (Sec 3.2, Eq.3-7) to avoid contradictory or duplicated persona facts, relevant to MF's FIDELIDAD anchor on single-source-of-truth per fact.
